questions.q: Which network does a container join if it's started without a `--network` flag?
options: none -- new containers have no networking by default
host -- new containers share the host's network stack by default
bridge -- Docker's default network
Docker refuses to start a container without an explicit network
questions.explain: bridge is Docker's default network. Every container so far in this course has landed there automatically, without anyone requesting it by name.

questions.q: What does the `host` network driver do?
options: Creates a fully isolated internal network with its own IP range
Disables all networking for the container
Lets the container share the host machine's network stack directly, with no isolation
Automatically resolves container names to IP addresses
questions.explain: host mode skips Docker's network isolation entirely -- the container uses the host's own network stack directly, unlike the isolated bridge network.

questions.q: What does `docker network inspect bridge` show?
options: Only the names of images currently running, not networking details
The network's subnet and which containers are attached to it, including each one's IP address
A list of every port published on the host
The contents of each container's filesystem
questions.explain: docker network inspect returns details about the network itself -- its subnet -- along with the containers attached and the IP address each one was assigned.

questions.q: On the default bridge network, what happens when `catalog` tries to reach `catalog-db` by its container name instead of its IP address?
options: It works exactly the same as using the IP address
It fails -- the default bridge network routes traffic by IP but doesn't resolve container names
It automatically falls back to using the host network
Docker returns an error and refuses to let the containers communicate at all
questions.explain: The default bridge network does route traffic between containers by IP, but it has no built-in DNS resolution for container names -- pinging by name fails even though pinging the IP succeeds.

questions.q: Why is relying on a container's IP address a fragile way for two containers to communicate?
options: IP addresses on the bridge network never actually work for container-to-container traffic
Docker reassigns a new IP address whenever a container is removed and recreated, breaking anything that hardcoded the old one
IP addresses are encrypted and cannot be used in application configuration
Containers on the bridge network are not allowed to have IP addresses at all
questions.explain: Container IPs on the default bridge network aren't stable across the container's lifecycle -- recreating a container gets it a new IP, so anything hardcoded to the old address breaks.
